messages:
Lina (Support): heads up — acme-app reported streaming responses getting cut off when routed through their grpc-web gateway. customer says SSE events arrive partially (first few events) then connection closes, client reconnects and then only gets a subset. they see extra billing for the reconnects too. ticket #CS-4821.
acme-app-team: repro steps we use: connect to https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream with our grpc-web proxy in front. client gets 3 events then socket closed. on reconnect we get a 401 once (token rotated) and then a new stream with only new events, but some server-side finalization event is missing. logs attached in the ticket (snippet below).
acme-app-team: log: 
```
[2026-02-26T15:12:01Z] upstream: accept conn id=57
[2026-02-26T15:12:02Z] upstream: write 512 bytes -> ok
[2026-02-26T15:12:03Z] upstream: write 128 bytes -> ok
[2026-02-26T15:12:03Z] upstream: client disconnected (broken pipe)
[2026-02-26T15:12:03Z] gateway: transformed h2->h1, buffered 640 bytes
```
acme-app-team: also we saw a 401 on reconnect (token rotated by auth server).
Lina (Support): thanks, can you share request/response headers (esp any X- or proxy headers) and confirm Content-Type on the responses? also does the client use fetch/curl or a browser grpc-web shim?
acme-app-team: client is browser using grpc-web shim. responses are Content-Type: text/event-stream. Headers from gateway: 
```
content-type: text/event-stream
transfer-encoding: chunked
x-forwarded-proto: https
x-grpc-web: 1
```
Jasper (Eng Runtime): likely interplay of grpc-web gateway rewriting HTTP/2 server push/stream semantics into HTTP/1.1 chunked responses. some gateways buffer until a threshold or until they see a connection close. if the gateway buffers, SSE semantics break (events need flushing). also token rotation causing 401 during reconnect can make the client start a fresh session — that explains duplicate billing.
Maya (Infra): we had a similar case where nginx default proxy_buffering caused entire response to be buffered. workaround was to set `X-Accel-Buffering: no` / `proxy_buffering off` for the upstream. grpc-web proxies sometimes have a `--stream-accept`/`--stream` flag to avoid buffering.
Jasper (Eng Runtime): immediate triage checklist: 1) confirm whether the gateway turns on response buffering for grpc-web translation. 2) check if it adds Content-Length (it shouldn't for streaming). 3) capture h2 vs h1 traces between gateway and origin. 4) reproduce with a minimal client that keeps auth stable (avoid token rotation during test).
Lina (Support): acme, can you try direct-to-origin (bypass grpc-web) with an http2 client? quick curl test: 
```
# from a machine that speaks HTTP/2
curl -v --http2-prior-knowledge "https://origin.redwood.internal/v1/stream?session=test" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <stable-token>" -N
```
this will show whether origin streams correctly. use `-N` to not buffer.
acme-app-team: ok will try, but we need a short-term mitigation. users see partial output during peak traffic and billing spikes. any ideas? :cry:
Jasper (Eng Runtime): short-term: 1) disable buffering on the grpc-web gateway (or set streaming mode). 2) ensure origin is flushing after every SSE event (send `\n\n` and flush). 3) add `Cache-Control: no-transform` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no`. 4) if you can't disable buffering, add an idempotent `session_id` query param so billing can dedupe reconnects.
Maya (Infra): also watch the gateway's chunk-size heuristics — if it aggregates small writes into larger chunks the browser may not render intermediate SSEs. forcing small writes or a timer-based flush every 200ms helps.
acme-app-team: billing issue — we got charged for 3 reconnects in a 30s window for one logical stream. is there a way on Redwood side to avoid counting reconnects as full new streams?
billing-bot: automated note — current billing counts requests per distinct HTTP handshake. we can add a mitigation: accept an `X-Stream-Session` header (opaque id) that will map reconnects to same session for a 60s window, billing team can treat them as a single session for billing. to enable, file an enterprise request with `billing@redwood` (we can do a case-by-case config).
Lina (Support): I filed an internal hotfix request with billing to allow session dedupe for this customer temporarily.
Jasper (Eng Runtime): longer-term: runtime should detect proxied h2->h1 adapters and set `flush` semantics on the socket or emit periodic keep-alive SSE comments `:keepalive\n\n` to force proxies to stream. we should also add a metric that counts partial-close events where server sent finalization event but client disconnected before ack.
Maya (Infra): infra action items: 1) check grpc-web gateway flags for `--disable-buffering` or `--streaming-response`. 2) add nginx `proxy_buffering off` + `X-Accel-Buffering: no` for routes serving SSE. 3) confirm TLS keepalive settings.
acme-app-team: quick test result — bypass to origin with curl shows continuous events, no premature close. going through gateway reproduces cut after ~3 events. gateway vendor confirmed their default buffers until 64KB or connection close.
Lina (Support): good repro. next steps I've assigned: 
- Jasper (Eng Runtime): look at runtime for keepalive/comments and metric + recommend default headers we can return to clients (ETA 2d).
- Maya (Infra): validate and suggest exact gateway flags/config to disable buffering and share config snippet (ETA 24h).
- Billing: temporary session-dedupe enabled for CS-4821 (owner Lina).
Jasper (Eng Runtime): quick config snippet suggestion to send from origin if you can't change gateway: 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Cache-Control: no-transform, no-cache
X-Accel-Buffering: no

:data: connected\n\n
```
and emit `:keepalive\n\n` every 10s. that forces most intermediaries to flush.
acme-app-team: thanks — we'll toggle proxy buffering off and test. also will add session_id header to dedupe.
Lina (Support): marking as in-progress. labeling severity: P2 (customer impact + billing noise). will update CS ticket with repro and our config recommendations. :eyes:
oncall-bot: incident reminder - weekly review scheduled for streaming edge issues.
